market_context: United States; a ripe avocado half stored in the refrigerator
title: How long does half an avocado last in the refrigerator?

seo.title: How long does half an avocado last in the refrigerator?
seo.meta_description: A cut avocado half keeps best quality for about 1-2 days in the refrigerator. Limit air with tight wrapping or a small airtight container; citrus slows browning but does not preserve it indefinitely.
seo.search_intent: Explain how long a cut avocado half keeps refrigerated, how to slow browning and how to distinguish oxidation from spoilage.

excerpt: A practical quality window for a cut avocado half is about 1-2 days in the refrigerator. Keep it at 40°F (4°C) or below and minimize air against the cut surface. Lemon or lime can slow browning; the pit only protects the area it physically covers and is not a substitute for tight packaging.
content_html:
An avocado begins changing as soon as it is cut. Oxygen reaches the flesh, browning enzymes become active and a bright green surface can turn brown within hours. That visible change can make the fruit look older before it is actually spoiled.

A useful refrigerator window is about 1-2 days

Iowa State University Extension advises that cut avocado will last about 1-2 days in the refrigerator. Treat that as a best-quality guide rather than a minute-by-minute safety deadline.

Starting condition matters. Half of an avocado that was just ripe will generally hold up better than half of one that was already very soft. Refrigerate it promptly and keep the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below.

How to store the half for tomorrow

Leave the skin on and minimize contact between the cut flesh and air. A small airtight container works well, or press food-safe wrap directly against the exposed surface before refrigerating.

A light coating of lemon or lime juice can slow browning because the acidic environment interferes with some oxidation reactions. It mainly protects color for a short period; it does not turn a cut avocado into a long-storage food.

The pit is only a partial shield

Leaving the pit in the unused half can reduce the amount of flesh directly exposed to air, but only where the pit physically covers it. The California Avocado Commission explains that this is a surface-area effect, not a preservative property of the seed.

Tight packaging therefore matters much more than whether the pit stays in.

Brown is not automatically bad

Surface browning is primarily oxidation. If a thin brown layer appears the next day while the flesh underneath is green, smells normal and has its usual texture, you can trim or scrape that layer for quality and use the rest.

That is different from mold, a sour or fermented odor, unusual liquid, sliminess or widespread black deteriorated flesh. Those are reasons to discard it.

Keep the method simple

You do not need to submerge a cut avocado in water. Cold storage plus minimal air exposure is enough for the short window in which the fruit is at its best.

The low-waste habit

If you know you will use only half, cover the other half immediately and refrigerate it. Plan to eat it the next day or within roughly 1-2 days, rather than relying on tricks to stretch a highly perishable cut fruit for much longer.

faq.question: How long does a cut avocado half last in the fridge?
faq.answer: About 1-2 days is a practical best-quality guide when it is promptly refrigerated and tightly covered.

faq.question: Can you eat avocado after it turns brown?
faq.answer: A thin brown surface can be oxidation rather than spoilage. Trim it if desired and check that the remaining flesh has a normal smell and texture.

faq.question: Does leaving the pit in keep avocado fresh?
faq.answer: It only reduces air exposure on the area it covers. Tight packaging is more important.
